clue.text: Writer's work published after tide turns

indicators.note: the published work comes after the turned tide in the answer
a tide that turns flows back, so the word for it is read backwards

parts.note: the tide is the sea's rise and fall, so tide stands for sea
OP is the abbreviation of opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: A writer's book comes out once the tide has turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes AES from SEA. The definition carries the possessive, read as 'Writer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist was a writer of moral animal stories.

clue.text: Film director flared angrily, having difficulty with leading male

indicators.note: flaring angrily suggests a wild outburst, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or difficulty
a cock is the dominant male bird, the leader of the flock

explanation.surface: A film director loses his temper, struggling with the lead actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The British-born master of suspense directed Psycho and Vertigo.

clue.text: Most see alcoholic drink as potential shot in the arm?

indicators.note: most of the word see means it loses its final letter

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Most people see a stiff drink as a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine is injected, literally a shot in the arm, playing on the idiom for a boost.

clue.text: Under pressure to pass the ball in important match

indicators.note: in a down entry the following piece sits under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
in football to lay the ball off is to pass it to a teammate

explanation.surface: A footballer is told to pass under pressure in a big game.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding game that settles a tie or promotion is a crucial fixture.

clue.text: Port: chap drinks a litre, reeling

indicators.note: reeling, as if staggering backwards, says the whole string is turned round

parts.note: Sam is any man's name, a chap
laps means drinks as a cat does

explanation.surface: A dockside man knocks back a litre and staggers.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on Gran Canaria is a major Atlantic harbour.

clue.text: Reluctant to appear in underclothes

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the longer word underclothes

explanation.surface: Someone is shy of being seen in their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for unwilling, also spelt loath.

clue.text: Vintage form of transport put newfangled car in shade

indicators.note: newfangled suggests something made over in a new way, so these letters are recast

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new-style car is parked out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newfangled' rearranges CAR, IN and SHADE together; 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed seat carried on poles was a period way of being conveyed.

clue.text: Almost everyone scoffs noisily in this foreign location

indicators.note: almost means the word drops its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: noisily says the next piece is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: jeers means scoffs or mocks

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody eats loudly in this place abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' leaves AL from ALL; 'scoffs' looks like eating greedily but means mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Algeria is a North African city, a place abroad.

clue.text: Still responsible for such silly talk?

definitions.meaning: an illicit still produces bootleg spirits

explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled liquor comes from a still, and the word also means nonsense.

clue.text: Mum's precious saw

parts.note: mum means silence, and the 's is read as is
golden means precious or very valuable

explanation.surface: Mother's treasured cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb.

clue.text: Arranged page layout for non-glossy edition

parts.note: taken as written
matt describes a dull, non-shiny finish

explanation.surface: A designer set out a page for a print run on matt paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out text and pictures on a page is the job of formatting.

clue.text: Develop low, gruff sound

parts.note: to grow is to develop

explanation.surface: A deep, rough voice emerges.
explanation.definitionFit: A low guttural noise such as a dog makes in threat.

clue.text: Times reporter's additional item on English rural region

indicators.note: in an across entry the rest follows on after the English letter

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: a reporter speaks words, so the next piece is heard

parts.note: more as a noun means an extra, an additional amount

explanation.surface: A Times journalist files an extra piece about the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Times' the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorland national park in Somerset and Devon is countryside in England.

clue.text: Great Dane, perhaps, ensnared with difficulty

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is struggled with and twisted about, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A big dog is caught in a trap and struggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Dane' looks like the dog; it means an eminent Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish fairy-tale author is a famous Dane, one example of many.

clue.text: Money-spinning idea firstly adopted by academic board

indicators.note: being adopted by something means being taken into it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: prof is short for professor, an academic
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: firstly asks for just the opening letter of the word idea

explanation.surface: A university committee takes up a scheme that should earn money.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinning venture makes a good return, so it is lucrative.

clue.text: Show how to speak in public?

definitions.text: Show how to speak in public?

parts.words: Show how to speak in public?
parts.note: read as a demonstration, holding up how to speak out: the phrase for speechifying at length

explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length and pompously to an audience is an idiom for orating.

clue.text: Supporter welcoming team's new fashion in US town

indicators.note: welcoming means taking guests inside, so pieces go into the supporter

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
ton is an old word for the fashionable set, high style

explanation.surface: A fan of the team adopts a new look in an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts town is where the first shots of the American Revolution were fired.

clue.text: Lover of Eastenders perhaps said to be a cad

indicators.note: as said by Londoners from the East End, whose accent turns the vowel sound of the lover word

parts.note: a swain is a country lover or suitor

explanation.surface: A character from the soap is called a rotter.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, where the Cockney accent says 'swain' rather like 'swine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a contemptible, dishonourable man.

clue.text: Cabs return to right place

definitions.meaning: in surgery, the manual pushing back of a displaced organ or hernia

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural of a hire car and also a surgical term for restoring a displaced part.

clue.text: Caught in footwear that's a disgrace

indicators.note: in shows the caught letter sitting inside the footwear

parts.note: a sandal is a type of open shoe
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Being caught in the wrong shoes is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: A shocking affair that causes public outrage is a disgrace.

clue.text: Cows just entering marshy areas

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the just word goes inside the marshes

parts.note: fens are low marshy lands, as in eastern England
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: Cattle wander into the boggy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cows' looks like cattle but is a verb meaning intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to scare them into submission.

clue.text: Fishy sort a politician's hiding in shelter

indicators.note: hiding in a place means being inside it, so these letters go within the shelter

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter
Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A suspicious type, a politician, is lurking in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy sort' suggests a shady character; it is literally a kind of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish is one sort of fish.

clue.text: Women finally admitted to trendy, cultured get-together

indicators.note: being admitted to a place means being let inside it

parts.note: hep is old slang for trendy, in the know

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of Women

parts.note: arty means showily cultured

explanation.surface: Women are let into a fashionable, artistic gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A party for a bride and her female friends is a social gathering.

clue.text: Description of teetotaller hooked by large amount of claret?

definitions.text: Description of teetotaller hooked by large amount of claret?

indicators.note: hooked by means caught inside, so the abstainer letters go within
a large amount of the word means most of it, losing the last letter

parts.note: claret is slang for blood, especially in boxing
TT stands for teetotal

explanation.surface: A sober drinker is caught out by a lot of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large amount of' leaves BLOO from BLOOD. The whole clue also describes the state of anyone hooked on claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has drunk plenty of red wine is completely drunk.

clue.text: Extended area of land with paths? One might say so

indicators.note: one saying it means it is spoken, so the next piece is heard not spelt

parts.note: tracked means having tracks or paths

explanation.surface: A wide stretch of country is crossed by footpaths.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse of land or region of some size.

clue.text: Note pad

definitions.meaning: a musical note lowered a semitone
informal for an apartment or home

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a lowered musical note and an apartment.

clue.text: Exposed in public, defeated leader is removed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: routed means defeated heavily

explanation.surface: A beaten party leader is ousted and shamed publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have one's secret publicly revealed, especially sexuality, is to be exposed.

clue.text: Hoarding money acquired company directors…

parts.note: a bill is a banknote, money, in American usage
the board is a company's directors

explanation.surface: Money is stockpiled by a firm's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoarding' looks like stockpiling; it is the large outdoor sign.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a hoarding is a large outdoor advertising board.

clue.text: …extremely charitable type is prone to giving half away

parts.note: kind means a type or sort
lies means is lying down, prone

indicators.note: giving half away keeps only the first half of the word to

explanation.surface: A very generous person tends to donate half of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link to the previous clue only in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative means most generous or benevolent.

clue.text: Artist releases his second single, a colossal one

indicators.note: single is the letter I, and the artist drops his second one

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A singer puts out a second single and has a huge hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a pop record; single is I, a Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant of Greek myth, so anything enormous.
